fixed.explanation: The single-block fast path in BlockManager.fast_xs returns a strided view of the block's 2D values. When the block is a temporary produced by selecting non-adjacent columns, the row Series keeps the whole (n_cols x n_rows) temporary alive. Copying the row (just n_cols values) makes the result own its data; under copy-on-write this is semantically safe.

query.intent: DataFrame.loc/iloc tuple indexing with a scalar row and a list of columns goes through the block manager's take/reindex of columns and then fetches a row via _ixs/xs, producing a Series whose values are a view (row slice) of a temporary 2D consolidated array. The row Series should be copied (or the interleaved values array made owning/contiguous) so it doesn't hold the large temporary base.
query.symptom: Selecting a single row with a non-adjacent list of columns returns a small Series whose data is a view into a large temporary (n_columns x n_rows) array, keeping much memory alive.
